article.title: The Rain Tree Avenue Journal
article.description: Patricia (64, retired teacher) & Neville D'Costa's (67, retired, church organist) Cantonment-loyal downsizing — a forty-building map, a boutique redevelopment with genuine monkey-tops, and a dignity fund explained once and never discussed again.
article.quote: "We're not against new Bengaluru. We just don't want to live there."

chatMessages.text: Riya, my dear, we've toured your boutique redevelopment twice now. And I'm obliged to report… it's rather good. Which is terribly inconvenient, because I'd prepared a whole speech against new construction. Footnotes and all.

Then let me argue your abandoned side so it's argued: the old building on Wheeler Road has soul, forty years of neighbours… and no sinking fund, one lift, and a roof that is — being generous — 'characterful.' The knee votes for the redevelopment, the orchids vote for the deep east balcony, and the monkey-tops are quoted from the original bungalow on that plot. The lane keeps its memory; you keep your lift.

realityChecks.title: The Repair-History-÷-Eight Arithmetic

realityChecks.title: The Tribe's Thinning

realityChecks.title: New Construction Inside the Old Fabric

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “The D'Costas are the keepers of a Bengaluru that exists now in pockets — and their map is measured in lanes and hymns, not corridors. Forty acceptable buildings in three square kilometres, struck through annually, watched like hawks. The uncomfortable irony — funded by the same assembly economics they mourn — was acknowledged and answered with one act of preservation: the church organ fund. And the boutique redevelopment surprised them: high ceilings, cross-ventilation, genuine monkey-tops quoted from the original bungalow, because the developer hired a conservation architect as a selling point. The knee voted redevelopment; the orchids voted for the east balcony. 'To new buildings… with old manners.' The dignity fund got its one line, and was never discussed again.”

chatMessages.text: The balcony faces east, the monkey-tops are genuine, and Thom's is a seven-minute walk. The fund has its sentence. I think we've finally kept a house without leaving home.

You didn't leave the Cantonment, ma'am — you carried it into a building with old manners and new walls. The lane keeps its memory; the tribe keeps its address; and the organ fund keeps the irony bearable. To new buildings with old manners.

tabs.adviceDescription: For heritage-quarter buyers, the edge is in treating scarcity as data: draw the living map, count the tribe honestly, and run the repair-history-divided-by-eight arithmetic before the charm. Accept that new construction inside the old fabric is now a premium product — and that the assembly economics that fund the move can be answered with one act of preservation. Let the knee and the orchids both vote, write the dignity fund's sentence once, and remember the purchase is about choosing which losses to refuse. The D'Costas proved the Cantonment travels — in monkey-tops, hymns, and a seven-minute walk to the bakery.
